notes:
Context: Oakbridge is a mid-stage biotech focused on clinical data indexing and QA for trial teams. They are exploring Redwood Private in a VPC/on-prem hybrid for PII/PHI workloads. Strong emphasis on auditability and long-term retention for regulatory review.

Most recent activity:
- 2026-02-18: Intro call w/ AE (Ethan), SE (Maya), and Oakbridge infra sec lead (L. Ramos). Fireflies id ff_2026-02-18_8472.
- 2026-02-25: Follow-up: Oakbridge sent internal SIEM sample (Splunk) + retention policy excerpt.
- 2026-03-01: Security sync — clarifications on KMS boundary and log egress.

Customer requirements (explicit):
- Full audit logging for all inference requests (request metadata, model id & version, token counts, latency, caller identity, route/fallback decisions).
- Access logs for control plane and data plane actions (who queried what, role, IP, timestamp).
- SIEM export: preferred Splunk HEC or syslog forwarder (customer wants push to their SIEM over TLS).
- Log schema: JSON structured events; top-level fields requested: event_id, ts_utc, tenant_id, user_id (nullable), client_ip, model_family, model_version, prompt_hash, response_digest, token_count_in, token_count_out, latency_ms, routing_decision, fallback_reason (if any), kv_cache_hit_rate, request_path, trace_id. Oakbridge provided sample mapping (attached in Drive).
- Retention: 7 years for audit trail per their regulatory counsel referencing FDA 21 CFR; 1-year high-fidelity (full prompts), 7-year hashed prompts and derived metadata only. Customer requests retention controls + tiered export API.
- KMS integration: customer-managed CMK in Azure Key Vault (want proof of in-transit and at-rest key control). Must support key rotation w/ no downtime and clear key-id logging.
- Residency: Primary data plane in us-east-2, with optional in-facility on-prem for PHI batch jobs.
- Security controls: SSO/SAML for console, audit logging pushed to SIEM in near-real-time, per-route RBAC, and immutable audit archive for regulatory inspection.

Questions raised by Oakbridge/security team:
- Can we stream real-time logs to Splunk HEC over customer-managed endpoint? (SE: yes, via log-forwarder; need network egress rules + approved certs)
- How does Redwood sign/verify log immutability for 7-year archive? (SE: support append-only object store + signed manifests; need legal language)
- What is the schema for prompt hashing / reversible data? Can Redwood ensure prompt content is hashed with salt controlled by Oakbridge KMS? (SE: architecture proposed: salt stored in CMK-protected vault; hashing step documented)
- Will KMS key usage appear in audit logs with key-id? (SE: yes — include key_id, operation, requestor in control-plane audit events)

POC scope proposed:
- Deliver Redwood Private in VPC with SIEM forwarder to customer Splunk test HEC endpoint.
- Implement audit schema v1 (fields above) and retention lifecycle: 1y raw, 7y hashed/metadata.
- Demo KMS integration using Oakbridge CMK (rotate once during POC).
- Run two-week load test focused on access-log volume and export throughput.

Risks and open items:
- Legal wants explicit clause about hashed-prompt non-reversibility — need legal to sign off w/ proposed hashing + salt model.
- Network architecture: customer requires egress only to specific HEC endpoints; Redwood network team needs ACLs and cross-tenant routing doc.
- Cost sensitivity: heavy logging will increase storage + egress; customer asked for Optimize recommendations to reduce token-level logging while preserving auditability.
